name: Membership and Proper Equivalence Queries Complexity of Addressing
proof: The $r=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ membership queries at the bit points reveal the injective code of the target, so $r$ queries suffice.  For the lower bound, against every failed proper equivalence query the adversary returns the proposed hypothesis's address point, which excludes only that hypothesis.  At any fixed transcript of $m$ membership answers and $p$ such failures, at most $2^m(p+1)\leq2^{m+p}$ targets can have been distinguished.  Thus identifying all $n$ targets requires $m+p\geq\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ queries.
references: Direct calculation from the addressing construction of \cite{maass1992lower}
